credible_improvement_required.rationale: Removing intermediate indices, mapping launches and copies is a credible mechanism. The explicit source/build/dispatch inspection can establish a useful baseline delta before implementation. Comparing identical selectors with separate versus fused mapping isolates fusion from selector replacement. Unmeasured critical-path exposure is a valid first falsification question.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: The reported Hopper integration provides a plausible port path, and the proposal covers raw-index fallback, ordering, block64 boundaries, causal bounds and graph replay. However, the dependency implementation, installed SM90 build, destination consumer contracts and final ordering behavior are unavailable. DeepSelect #14 supplies an explicit SM90 build lead; its BF16 cluster results do not establish eligibility of this particular integration.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: The three-arm comparison, eligible-call denominator, all-rank telemetry, native workloads, separate profiling, held-out diagnostics and alternating full-run confirmation distinguish selector and fusion effects. Support/reject/inconclusive rules are appropriate. Useful-gain margins, quality tolerances and adequate opportunity coverage still need operational definitions.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: Observed supplied artifact: #41561 identifies the runtime file, integration contract and test-review history. Author claim: "Write transformed int32 KV slots directly into the existing output buffer." Its H20 region benchmark reports approximately 163–165 to 31–32.5 microseconds at widths 32K/128K and 1–32 rows; this combines selector replacement and mapping changes. Transfer inference: eliminating exposed mapping work may benefit H200 serving. Final dependency code, benchmark input dtype and H200 effect remain unknown.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: A narrow guarded port with native fallback complements the compute and communication candidates. Inspection is inexpensive, and diagnostic-only gains are explicitly separated from primary-workload value. Integration effort and primary eligible-call frequency remain unknown; the source's wide-logit benchmarks do not establish exposure under native 8K-prefix traffic.

objections: The source benchmark cannot establish the incremental benefit of page-mapping fusion; the selector-only comparator is essential.

The review phrase "testing no real functionality" concerns two mocked tests. The same excerpt also describes real kernel-through-call-site coverage; dropping mocks does not establish that all integration coverage is absent.
FlashInfer #5889 supplies a competing fused-page-output API and H100 microbenchmark claims. Its target eligibility should be checked before committing to a custom DeepSelect port.
vLLM #41105 is a relevant baseline-membership lead, but its supplied title does not prove equivalent fusion is installed or active.
reviews.required_revision: Defer qualification despite a weighted score of 76/100 because the applicability gate is unknown. Pin the operator and integration revisions, identify the destination call sites and actual dtype/width/K/ordering contracts, and resolve build and graph requirements. Include the supplied FlashInfer alternative in the cheap eligibility check. Preserve the three-arm attribution and distinguish prompt length from indexer-logit width.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Shape-appropriate GEMM configurations can plausibly reduce exposed execution time without changing formats. The proposed parity and shape-dispatch inspection is a legitimate inexpensive gate. A versus S0 separates engine choice, while S0 versus S1 targets configuration changes. The bundle's large reported improvement is correctly excluded as a prediction of tuning-only value.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: H200 execution is author-reported, but under TP8/EP1 and materially different checkpoint, Engram and replay settings. No pinned matched SGLang build or implementation evidence establishes the required TP1/DP4/EP4, host Engram, FP8 KV and real DSpark semantics together. The parity checklist is sound; whether its requirements can be met remains unknown.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: The three contrasts, disjoint calibration, shape-level dispatch counters, final-rank prefix attribution and held-out sessions address major confounders. Full-run pairing and separate profiling follow the contract. Clarify the configuration search space: S1 is itself a fixed configuration set, so its distinction from the 'best existing fixed' S0 comparator must be reproducible. Add a separate decision for an engine-only win.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: Observed artifact: the startup excerpt reports "Using 'MARLIN' Mxfp4 MoE backend." This covers one worker's selection, not all-rank execution. Author claim: #41251 reports output-throughput/GPU ratios of 2.0574–2.3498 across "three alternating paired sweeps" on eight H200s with random 8192/1024 traffic. Transfer inference: configuration tuning could help target shapes. The supplied excerpt does not expose the proposed JSON changes or dispatch implementation, so their isolation from BF16 expansion is unverified; source speculation settings and isolated tuning effect are unknown.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: This supplies complementary compute coverage and potentially useful engine-comparison information. The cheap parity gate avoids premature migration work. However, a second engine environment, equivalent telemetry and exact deployment semantics may dominate effort. Integration duration, startup overhead, memory headroom and primary-workload benefit remain unknown.

objections: The H200 bundle comparison does not identify which configurations changed, which target shapes would select them, or how much benefit survives without weight expansion and other fusions.
S0 has no concrete revision or verified configuration-only ablation in the supplied packet. Merely naming a future pinned control does not establish readiness.

SGLang #40417 reports that a seemingly better shape estimate regressed serving. It concerns a different Humming path and cannot veto dense-GEMM tuning, but it reinforces the need to validate actual lookup keys, routing and graph-tier behavior.
The multi-node deadlock in #40744 motivates collective-participation checks; it does not establish failure of two independent EP4 replicas.
If S0 beats vLLM while S1 adds nothing, the current combined support rule should not erase the independently useful engine result.
reviews.required_revision: Defer qualification: weighted score 68/100 and applicability unknown. Supply a concrete SGLang revision, a verified parity matrix and the exact configuration-only diff with dispatch consumers. Define the static comparator's search space and calibration budget. Record independent engine and tuning decisions, while preserving transport, numeric recipe, topology and speculative semantics for matched comparisons.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Overlapping token preparation with outstanding remote stores is a credible dispatch mechanism. Checking effective transport, patch inclusion, connectivity and adapter compatibility before implementation meets the baseline-delta requirement. Backend activation and pipeline modification are separated, with both matched-geometry and calibrated unmodified comparators. Remote exposure can legitimately be measured during first falsification.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: The supplied H100 implementation is a plausible Hopper transfer lead, and buffer-lifetime, graph, token-identity and distributed checks are well scoped. The pinned engine's elastic adapter, Marlin payload compatibility, workspace requirements and actual peer connectivity remain unknown. DeepEP #763 adds a concrete version restriction: "Migrate from ElasticBuffer to the dedicated buffer APIs." No target dependency inventory resolves which API generation applies.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: A/B/C staging separates backend activation from buffering; remote rows/bytes, eligible dispatches, geometry controls and exposed timing distinguish bandwidth gains from serving gains. Both replicas, skewed routing, empty ranks, graph replay and run-level confirmation are covered. Add an independent B-versus-A decision so a useful unmodified backend is retained if triple buffering ties or regresses. Explicitly track workspace growth and its effect on usable KV capacity.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: Observed supplied artifact: #693 contains code/review excerpts defining three NVLink buffers and discussing tma_store_wait<1>(), plus the warning "the two sources of truth diverge". Author results are eight-H100 remote-only averages: dispatch 250 to 280 GB/s, or 203 to 220 GB/s at imbalance 1.5; combine is unchanged. Transfer inference is reduced exposed dispatch time, potentially offset by shared-memory pressure and the 14-warp cap. Payload dimensions, numeric format, repetitions, variance and H200 serving effects are unknown.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: Communication coverage is complementary, and the inspection-first stop plus backend rollback are practical. Adapter work, API migration and graph-safe buffer validation may be substantial. Four-rank locality and concurrent expert computation can erase remote-only gains. Cost remains correctly parameterized, but integration effort and memory impact are unknown.

objections: A generic DeepEP backend option does not establish that the elastic direct-NVLink kernel is reachable. The exact dependency and adapter revisions are essential.
DeepEP #763 changes APIs and lists CUDA/NCCL requirements; #605 describes a new GEMM layout. Neither source establishes that the proposed path can preserve the installed Marlin contract.
The Humming-specific grouped-GEMM restriction in vLLM #59488 is not evidence that Marlin is compatible or incompatible with this adapter.
The source's buffer-reuse warning identifies an invariant requiring verification, not a demonstrated failure of the proposed repaired port.

SGLang #23896 has conflicting summary and raw results and changes speculation. It supplies no reliable causal estimate of a DeepEP regression. #18519's successful workaround removes DeepEP and does not demonstrate a fix.
reviews.required_revision: Defer qualification despite a weighted score of 74/100 because applicability is unknown. Pin compatible B/C dependency revisions and identify the exact adapter, payload layout and graph/workspace contract. Resolve the shared buffer-count definition and reuse invariant. Keep API/toolchain migration attributable, estimate workspace effects before execution, and issue separate backend-activation and triple-buffering decisions.

global_gaps: All three proposals have credible research mechanisms; none has an established constraint violation warranting a failed required gate. All remain deferred on target applicability. Weighted totals cannot override an unknown gate, and no measured H200 speedup is required to begin the proposed eligibility checks.

Observed evidence here consists of supplied source and runtime excerpts. Performance figures remain attributed author results. Target bottlenecks, all-rank attention/MoE dispatch, effective allgather_reducescatter transport and candidate effects remain unknown. Source hashes, patch availability metadata and prior ranking prose do not establish current deployment membership.

Before later experiments, resolve G01–G05 definitions, preregister useful-gain and quality margins, define adequate activation coverage, and specify counter-reset handling, failure/truncation denominators and bounded run budgets. Verify the evaluator environment and profiler clean-marker integration separately. The production SLO is unknown; provisional diagnostic thresholds cannot establish production qualification.
The full eight-GPU hourly price is unknown. Retain parameterized cost using elapsed seconds and exact output tokens, with qualified-output cost reported separately.

The rubric requests five selections, while the supplied draft and brief contain three candidates. These three cover selection, compute and communication, but do not establish a complete five-item portfolio. The repository list contains 15 names despite references to 13; supplied IDs and title-only leads do not demonstrate exhaustive engineering review.

Reported facts in the three cards are substantially supported as attributed claims. Untested transfer predictions are not factual failures. Missing final implementation evidence, unresolved source revisions and omitted corpus records remain evidence gaps.
